svg.title: Men's cadet semi-formal coat, wearer's right sleeve laid flat (outer arm toward the viewer, plain Class A cuff, no braid), for NCO chevrons
svg.metadata: {"asset_id":"garment-semiformal-class-a-coat-male-sleeve-flat-right","name":"Men's cadet semi-formal coat, wearer's right sleeve laid flat (outer arm toward the viewer, plain Class A cuff, no braid), for NCO chevrons","size_in":{"w":7.4969,"h":26.93},"units":"1 user unit = 0.01 in","viewBox":[0,0,749.69,2693],"size_source":"measured","size_basis":"Measured on the sheet's own sleeve (garment-semiformal-class-a-coat-male, which shares the Class A coat sheet, outline and scale; outline jacket_male.webp (581x719 px) traced at 0.0474 in/px, scaled x1.0882 to true size (coat-scale.js)), straightened, then widened from the hanging view to the flat. Length 26.69 in = the outer edge's arc length from the shoulder seam point (the top of the armhole seam) down the drawn outline to the cuff's outer corner (the sheet's vertical drop is 26.05 in). Widths: a hanging sleeve seen from the front shows its diameter (circumference / pi); laid flat it measures circumference / 2, so each flat width = the hanging width measured on the sheet (square to the sleeve axis) x pi/2 = 1.5708. Hanging widths: full cap 4.66 in (the widest up to the elbow; the hanging sleeve is hidden under the shoulder, so its drawn width at the seam itself is 0), elbow 4.40 in (55 percent of the length, 14.68 in down), cuff edge 3.46 in (corner to corner as drawn, 11.61, 29.53 to 8.16, 29.29 in the sheet's frame). Flat widths: cap 7.32 in, elbow 6.92 in, cuff 5.43 in. Cross-check: a men's 40R service coat sleeve is about 16 in around at the bicep, so about 8 in flat; the measured cap of 7.32 in flat is a 14.6 in circumference at the sheet's fullest point, in line with it. Box 7.50 x 26.93 in = sleeve plus 0.12 in on every
